title: The robe not passed on
hook: Huineng said the robe would no longer be handed down; the teaching itself is the proof

segments.voice: Yesterday, sudden awakening, and the sutra's reminder that the teaching itself has no speeds. Your line: sudden and gradual. Whose different pace did you make room for? Day one thousand two hundred nineteen.

Some families have one object that matters more than everything else in the house. A watch. A ring. A recipe card in a grandmother's handwriting. It's meant to be handed down, a sign that the line goes on. And some families know the other side of that story: the cousins who stopped speaking over who got the watch. The thing that was meant to hold the family together became the thing it split over. Chan had an object like that too: a robe, handed from teacher to student. And in the Platform Sutra, someone decides it should stop. Today: the robe not passed on.
screen: `ONE OBJECT THAT MATTERS.` → `A SIGN THE LINE GOES ON.` → `THE THING THEY SPLIT OVER.`

segments.voice: First, the night it's given. After the two verses on the wall, the sutra says, Hongren calls Huineng in secret, teaches him, and hands him the robe and bowl as the sign of the teaching. Then he tells him to leave that same night and go south, because people may try to harm him. He also says, in paraphrase: the robe has become a cause of strife. Let it stop with you. Second, the chase. Monks set off after Huineng to take the robe back. One of them, a former military officer named Huiming, catches up at a mountain pass. Huineng lays the robe on a rock and steps aside. In the sutra, Huiming tries to pick it up and cannot lift it. Third, what Huiming says next. He tells Huineng: I came for the teaching, not for the robe. And Huineng gives him one, in paraphrase: not thinking of good, not thinking of evil, right at this moment, what is your original face? Huiming, the sutra says, awakens on the spot. The man who ran up a mountain for a piece of cloth goes home with something nobody can carry off. Fourth, the end of the line. Late in the sutra, near the end of his life, Huineng tells his students the robe will not be handed down. The proof that the teaching is alive won't be an object anyone can fight over. It will be the teaching itself, showing up in the people who practice it. The robe stops here, so that the teaching doesn't have to.
screen: `ROBE AND BOWL, AT NIGHT.` · `A CHASE TO THE MOUNTAIN PASS.` · `I CAME FOR THE TEACHING.` · `THE TEACHING IS THE PROOF.` · then, large: `THE ROBE STOPS HERE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like. Sit and let the breath settle. Bring to mind one thing you know how to do that could never be handed over in a box. How to apologize properly. How to wait for the bread to rise. How to sit with someone who's grieving. Notice where it lives: in the hands, in the timing, in the voice. Nobody could lay it on a rock, and nobody could carry it off. Then think of one person who might pick it up, today or soon. Not by being given anything. Just by seeing you do it. The bell holds the time.
The robe not passed on. In the Platform Sutra, the robe that had become a cause of strife stops with Huineng, and the teaching itself carries on. Today's word.
screen: `THE ROBE NOT PASSED ON — today's word`.

segments.voice: Your line: the robe stops here. Today, pass on one thing you were taught, by doing it, not by handing anything over. Day one thousand two hundred nineteen.

screen: `DAY 1219 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: MEDITATION AND WISDOM ARE ONE.`

howItsDone: Zen and Chan schools speak of the teaching passing from teacher to student, often called mind-to-mind transmission, and the story of Huiming at the mountain pass is often retold, with 'original face' used as a koan.

notes: Versions differ. Check: Hongren's 'the robe is a source of strife; let it stop with you' (衣為爭端，止汝勿傳) is in the later (Zongbao) text; Huiming as a former military officer; the robe on the rock he could not lift (retold version); 'not thinking of good, not thinking of evil... original face' (later text); Huineng's late statement that the robe will not be handed down.

Editor pass: Huiming is a former military officer (a general) in the later text, not a soldier; the unliftable robe is in the Zongbao text itself, so 'in the version often retold' became 'in the sutra'; reworked the practice so it no longer repeats day 1204's give-thanks-to-a-teacher practice and stays on a teaching that can't be carried off.
